To validate the model, we utilized a large dataset of 68 electrophysiological experiments on the dorsal striatum in marmoset monkeys, successfully recreating a wide range of electrophysiological phenomena with our model, including oscillatory activities induced by different frequencies of cortical input, the release of glutamate caused by action potentials, and the firing rates of various neuron types in response to different levels of dopamine. Furthermore, our model exhibits a high degree of sensitivity to changes in the concentration of dopamine and other critical neurotransmitters and ions. With this model, we were able to predict the efficacy of optogenetic stimulation and chemical interventions such as dopamine replacement therapy on the dorsal striatum in marmoset monkeys, providing a fundamental framework for the exploration of Parkinson's disease mechanisms and the evaluation of potential treatments

The proliferation of mobile devices and online map platforms demands high-performance visualizations of large-scale maps. The traditional vector map rendering technique is effective but inefficient when rendering detailed maps due to the high frequency of line segments being rendered. This frequency leads to a notable slowdown in performance, particularly in areas with dense line segment concentrations, such as city centers. The line rendering process, specifically the formation of joints between line segments, significantly contributes to this slowdown. To mitigate this issue, a novel AA (anti-aliasing) technique for line joins has been developed, reducing performance costs in urban areas by as much as 40% and overall AA rendering time by 24% on mobile devices and 30% on PCs.

Our team utilized the KOOLS-IFU on Seimei Telescope for integral field unit (IFU) observations of 9 ultra/luminous infrared galaxies located close to our own (z < 0.04) and participating in the GOALS survey. These targets span a broad spectrum of merger phases, from early stages to advanced. With the IFU data we collected, we successfully isolated several distinct emission lines including hydrogen beta, oxygen III at wavelength 5007, hydrogen alpha at wavelength 6563, double-ionized nitrogen at wavelength 6549-6583, and sulfur II at wavelength 6717-6731. Our analysis with spectral resolutions ranging between 1500 to 2000 allowed us to derive spatially resolved ionized gas maps as small as 200-700 parsecs, as well as active galactic nucleus (AGN) diagnostics within 3-11 kiloparsecs of our targets. Our data showed a correlation between active galactic nuclei and the outflow of gas as oxygen III at wavelength 5007 from our targets, exhibiting velocities between -1436 and -81 kilometers per second. Furthermore, we discovered a velocity difference of up to 629 kilometers per second within the 2.5-57 kiloparsec range around our targets, indicating a potential rotation of the gas. Our results also indicated a broad hydrogen alpha at wavelength 6563 spectrum in one target, suggesting an outflow of gas in that particular galaxy.

The multivariate interpolation operator is typically constructed using piecewise linear functions to approximate absolute differences between values. A novel, transcendental interpolation function is derived from the hyperbolic tangent, providing a more precise approximation of the absolute difference. The derivative of this function is infinity at zero, which poses a challenge in interpolation theory. To address this issue, a gentle approximation is developed by inserting a smooth curve around the origin. The proposed interpolation function is used in a quasi-interpolation operator framework, demonstrating improved performance compared to traditional methods. The implementation is efficient, with a minimum computational overhead equivalent to $O(n)$ operations. The paper also explores the convergence properties of the proposed operator, showing that it meets the requirements of a Korovkin type theorem. The advantages of the novel interpolation function are particularly beneficial in shape preserving applications, including smooth and non-smooth cases, with an example given involving the solution of a nonlinear partial differential equation.

A novel dataset of categorized weather images has been introduced, containing 9 distinct conditions which were not previously addressed by existing research. This dataset, comprising 9600 high-quality images, is unique in its large scale and diverse range of conditions. To enhance training efficiency, a cutting-edge data augmentation technique was employed, leveraging a unique combination of transformations. The effectiveness of this approach was validated across multiple CNN configurations, resulting in significant improvements over traditional methods. Notably, one experiment revealed that a simple Convolutional Neural Network achieved a remarkable 86.11% accuracy rate, outperforming previous weather classification models and demonstrating the promise of this approach for complex real-world applications.

In 2013, Convolution Recurrent Neural Networks were initially introduced for speech enhancement, offering a more balanced approach combining both temporal recurrent and frequency convolutional network properties. Since then, various audio enhancement models have adopted this dual approach, yielding superior results to previous methods. Notably, Dual-Path Convolution Recurrent Networks have emerged as a top-performing model in various evaluation metrics, delivering a more balanced and effective dual-path architecture. By integrating both global and local information using dual pathways, these networks produce a more accurate multi-scale representation of speech, effectively reducing artifacts and surpassing existing methods. In particular, the Dual-Path Convolution Recurrent Networks have been shown to significantly reduce the background noise and distortion of speech, outperforming other models in terms of PESQ, STOI, SFRA, and wideband extended short-time third-order covariance function measures.

A new statistics methodology is introduced, focused on the turn-around radii of cluster halos to break the degeneracy between $\Lambda$CDM, $f(R)$ gravity, and massive neutrinos cosmological scenarios. By utilizing the final positions of objects at the edge of halos instead of their internal dynamics, this method is highly sensitive to the impact of modified gravity and massive neutrinos on the expansion history of the universe. As a result, it is able to distinguish between the effects of these cosmological scenarios at the halo periphery, which is not possible with traditional dynamics-based methods. A preliminary analysis with the considered scenarios reveals distinct signatures on the distribution of turn-around radii. Furthermore, this study is a preliminary exploration of the new statistics with an ideal sample of high-quality, turn-around radii for a set of massive clusters.

Recently introduced multi-fluid models hold promise in refining the simulation of atmospheric convection within weather and climate simulations. A two-fluid model, which treats air and water vapor as distinct fluids, represents an initial simplification of the complex atmospheric composition. However, even this simplified model exhibits a high level of sophistication that demands extensive computational resources. In response, researchers are turning to single-column models as a cost-effective strategy for evaluating the multi-fluid approach. We have undertaken the modification of a single-column model to incorporate a multi-fluid model that includes an equation for the transport of water vapor, alongside typical air pressure, temperature, and horizontal wind velocity equations. The modified single-column model is used to conduct an experimental investigation into its predictive capabilities under both stable and unstable conditions. The results show that the model is capable of predicting the critical point for onset of convection, the depth of the convective layer, and heat flux patterns accurately across a range of Rayleigh-Benard experiments. Nonetheless, some deviations in the model's predictions for water vapor distribution highlight the need for further validation and improvement.

We investigate the possibility of securely entangling two distant atoms that do not start out in an an correlated state. A specific quantum light-mediated application achieves this through JC-JC interactions, aided by stationary mirror systems that modulate the entanglement of a shared quantum channel. The proposed system uses superposed light and stationary mirror configurations that allow for the implementation of various von Neumann operator transformations. Notably, this enables the creation of an arbitrary two-qubit entangling operation via unitary equivalence. The proposed system's efficacy is demonstrated in a scenario involving two two-level atoms connected by an optical fiber. The success of the protocol relies on the collection of a specific number of photon states from the output light, which serves as an indicator of entanglement creation. Furthermore, the proposed system can be extended to target specific Bell states and accommodate various types of qubit configurations.

The Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) is one of the primary detectors in the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN, tracking particle interactions resulting from high-energy collisions. As part of the CMS system, the silicon pixel detector forms the innermost component responsible for navigating the trajectory of particles. Although initially operational from 2009 to 2016, it has been replaced with an upgraded variant in 2017. During a preceding period of shutdown for the LHC, an upgraded forward pixel detector prototype featuring a novel readout system and third disk was introduced, integrating eight pilot blades built using advanced digital readout chips. Through pilot module testing, researchers obtained practical experience in operating the upgraded detector. This study reports the results of analyzing data captured with these new components, including a detailed explanation of the reconstruction process and associated calibration steps. Furthermore, it includes illustrations of the hit finding efficiency and track-hit residual patterns.

A key aspect of quantum field theory is the Kall\'en-Lehmann spectral representation, which addresses the internal structure of hadrons. For the SU(2) gluonium particle, a method is presented to extract the spectral function from correlation functions of the fundamental fields of the theory, specifically using the Schr\"odinger and Hamiltonian operators within the context of the SU(2 Yang-Mills theory. A notable finding reveals that the correlation function two-point function can be accurately determined using a limited set of low-momentum modes, resulting in a spectral function that displays the internal structure of the SU(2) gluonium and its excitations in a momentum-independent manner. Additionally, the lowest-energy state of the SU(2) gluonium is identified as a stable state rather than a set of unstable states and is characterized by a non-zero mass.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
organizations and individuals to track the public's emotions towards them and their rivals.
As a result, analyzing public sentiment has become both crucial and difficult to accomplish.
In this project, we gathered and manually annotated seven freely accessible Twitter sentiment
databases. We then compiled a new set of training and testing data from these sources. An
LSTM-based model was developed to determine the sentiment expressed in individual
tweets. The model's performance was assessed using the newly created dataset. The results
showed that even without any data augmentation, the model could accurately identify the
sentiment in new, unseen data with a high level of precision. Additionally, we observed
that using data augmentation techniques can improve the model's performance even further.

It's observed that the thermodynamic properties of an non-linear charged black hole in an Anti-de Sitter space are significantly affected by its non-linear interaction with external light. As certain light frequencies are absorbed, the system's temperature shifts, ultimately causing cyclic heat transfer. This process is described by an equation which relates the energy changes to both the absorbed energy and the new temperature. When the absorption rate is constant, this equation simplifies to a first law that accounts for the changes in both the black hole's temperature and its light field "shade".

The study of quantum systems' entanglement and the onset of their synchronization is highly intricate. Both phenomena exhibit complex interconnections, as seen in the significant alteration of entanglement during the transition from an asynchronous to a synchronized state. This study sheds light on the interplay between these phenomena by examining the tomographic representation of two-Mode Gaussian states. It demonstrates how changes in the Wigner function's structure, particularly those indicating a shift from asymmetric to symmetric form, can be utilized to identify the onset of synchronization by analyzing specific moments of the tomographic probability distribution. Furthermore, it shows that the fidelity of two-mode Gaussian states can serve as a reliable indicator for both entanglement and synchronization, and that this fidelity is directly correlated with the average photon number and coherent amplitude in the system.

Building a conversational AI system with a specific tone and purpose remains a challenging task in current natural language processing research. Although substantial progress has been made in dialogue systems and machine learning models that can understand and respond to human language, it is still difficult to create a system that can effectively engage in open-domain conversations with others. One key issue is the difficulty in restricting the system's responses to a particular personality or role. For example, a system designed for customer service interactions should be able to understand customer queries and provide relevant responses, but it's also important to prevent the injection of unwanted personality into the dialogue. One approach to achieving this is to modify the pre-trained language model to align it with the desired role, but this is a complex process due to the challenges of fine-tuning large models on specific datasets. Instead of relying on traditional machine learning methods, we propose using a set of simple rules and a role-specification prompt to target the desired personality or role. We also suggest using a method called role-aware response selection to filter out responses that don't match the desired personality or role. We tested our approach on a range of role-specification datasets and the results showed that our method outperformed the current state of the art in terms of accuracy. Furthermore, we were able to create a customer service chatbot using our approach, but the results were mixed and there were instances where the system provided incorrect responses to certain queries.

Effective evaluation of pest management strategies is crucial for growers, policymakers, and researchers in determining the most efficient methods for minimizing economic and environmental impacts. However, existing approaches to comparative assessments are marred by methodological flaws, uncertainty, and partiality, which can lead to misleading conclusions and biased outcomes. To address these issues, we introduce a reliable method for appraising treatments that leverages mathematical inequalities to account for measurement errors in yield data and a statistical test to determine the significance of differences. We further contend that traditional meta-analyses are prone to systematic errors and may yield contradictory results due to varying treatment effects among sites. Consequently, we advocate for site-specific assessments that consider the unique environmental conditions of each location. Our method is exemplified through a case study on strawberry disease management, wherein we investigate the comparative efficacy of several fungicide application schedules in controlling powdery mildew and improving yield.

360-degree virtual tourism videos enable travelers to explore destinations remotely. Many systems have been developed to process these videos by analyzing user perspectives. However, managing large numbers of possible perspectives becomes challenging due to the 360-degree nature of the content. To address this issue, our approach focuses on subtitles embedded within the video. We utilize a BERT-based model to determine the importance of each subtitle to that particular direction, relying on carefully curated datasets. Importance scores for each perspective are then calculated by combining the results of the importance of the subtitles appearing in that direction. Our evaluation shows that importance-based perspective determination outperforms traditional approaches, while reducing the number of possible perspectives by 90%.

Tensor network methods have commonly been used to compute the time-evolution of quantum many-body systems due to their balance of computational cost and accurate results. However, these techniques typically suffer from truncation errors that scale with the size of the region within the tensor network, hindering their application to strongly interacting systems over time. A new approach has been developed that overcomes this limitation by constructing approximate tensor networks specifically suited for thermal states and time-evolved systems, allowing for the precise representation of a local region of interest while enabling efficient contraction of the tensor network. This new approach is theoretically efficient, achieving a high degree of precision while minimizing computational costs, and is demonstrated through numerical examples involving thermal states and time-evolved systems. A key feature of this new approach is the formation of entanglement patterns that are directly linked to the system's time-evolution, providing a local perspective on the spread of entanglement.

We develop a decoupling theory for a diverse group of problems that incorporate nonlinear operators and non-isotropic domains. Our decoupling results are the foundation for the development of novel low-frequency local boundary estimates for pseudodifferential operators with non-isotropic smooth symbols within these diverse contexts. These boundary estimates are a crucial advancement, as they enable us to establish the desired approximable scale property, a crucial component for the development of new weak-type inequalities via the scale-based approximation approach.

In this study, we define anisotropic $p$-capacitance and demonstrate its equivalence to the anisotropic Minkowski inequality, establishing a direct relationship to the classical $p$-capacitance for isotropic spaces.

The Microscope space test for the weak equivalence principle involves measuring tiny differences in the acceleration of two test masses as they orbit the Earth. Certain random events known as glitches can compromise the measurement by producing unanticipated movements. This study investigates the impact of these events on the experiment's outcome and explores methods to mitigate their effect by employing optimized data processing techniques. By limiting the intensity of glitches, the test mass acceleration gap can be narrowed to a value of $2.5 \times 10^{-19}$ $m/s^2$ within a 95% confidence interval, thus minimizing the influence of glitches to an insignificant fraction of the measurement uncertainty.

We examine dynamic colloidal pairs suspended in flow that pass through a narrow channel, where we measure the time-dependent separation distance and the impact of hydrodynamics on pair interaction. Due to adhesive forces between the particles, they often bond at contact, and we investigate various time scales as the particles release from this stuck state. When the flow rate is moderate, the particles exhibit an oscillating behavior around their bonded position, while more vigorous flow causes them to repeatedly collide and move apart. The distance between the particles is determined by a balance between adhesive forces and the hydrodynamic pressure that pushes them apart. We find that at high flow rates, the particles' behavior is similar to that in steady-state conditions, but at lower flow rates, the particles release energy from their bond and move apart due to their vibration. This energy is used to overcome the adhesive force, and we show that it arises from both the hydrodynamic pressure and the conversion of kinetic energy. This finding is relevant to research on colloid dynamics under flow, and we suggest that both energy sources should be considered.

The problem of determining k shortest path union collection (KSPUC) has gained significant interest in recent years due to its numerous applications in transportation systems, biology, and other fields, and has been an open problem since 2008. The study defines a new concept, strongest path union collection (SPUC), which includes k shortest path union collection as a special case, and proposes methods for computing SPUC on series, parallel, and series-parallel graphs. Furthermore, the study establishes upper and lower bounds for the computational complexity of SPUC on these types of graphs, and demonstrates efficient algorithms for computing k shortest path union collection on certain graph classes, such as series and parallel graphs. The study also examines lower and upper bounds for the computation of SPUC on general graphs, and provides a new upper bound for the k shortest path union collection problem on general graphs, solving a long-standing open problem. The study also investigates upper and lower bounds for the computation of SPUC on undirected graphs, and provides a new upper bound for the k shortest path union collection problem on undirected graphs, solving a new open problem. The study also examines upper and lower bounds for the computation of SPUC on directed graphs with vertices having more than one connection.

The impact of infrared renormalons in the color dipole gluon distribution's variance is being quantified, and calculations demonstrate how non-linear small-x saturation impacts shift the Borel plane's initial IR pole from $2/\beta_2$ to $1/\beta_2$, thereby changing the estimated uncertainty to approximately $\chi^2=1$ times the power variation, with a specific value of two times the mean squared deviation. This increased uncertainty is expected to be observable in LHCb's predicted outputs, with shifts of up to 20 ns in the mean lifetime and 5 GeV in the mass of heavy mesons.

As the number of frogs per site grows, the frog model's behavior shifts from transient to recurrent on a d-ary rooted tree. We demonstrate that this critical frog density is directly correlated with the tree's degree.

Researchers are focusing on extremely thin alloys of iron and rhodium to create a unique three-dimensional lattice that reacts differently to light and a magnetic field. Studies have shown that when an ultrafast laser heats this alloy, it generates a strong magnetic field that can be influenced by light. If light with a specific polarization is directed at a particular angle, it can produce a massive increase in light emitted. This emission boost is most noticeable when the light's angle is nearly 90 degrees to the alloy's surface. It has also been found that changing the light's polarization can increase the amount of light emitted by as much as five times. This phenomenon occurs at extremely low temperatures, around 10 Kelvin. It was discovered that light can increase the amount of time the alloy spends in a magnetic state, ultimately leading to a greater impact on light emission. It is suggested that this effect could be used to improve the performance of light-based systems at very low temperatures.

Knowledge acquisition in limited-label settings is a persistent challenge in large-scale machine learning projects. A significant amount of data is often required to train models in a supervised manner, which can be time-consuming and costly. This paper introduces an innovative approach to overcome this constraint by leveraging a small amount of data to train a black-box model that makes decisions for a target task. The key innovation lies in using a transformation-based method that enables the efficient transfer of knowledge from the black-box model to a set of diverse, high-capacity models through shared latent variables. This approach is particularly notable for its zero-shot knowledge transfer capability, as it allows the target models to learn from the black-box model without being exposed to the target labels. Our experiments demonstrate the efficacy of this approach on complex datasets, showcasing a notable improvement over the current state-of-the-art methods in limited-label settings.

Researchers have observed two rare phi meson productions, $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ and $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$, at the LHCb experiment within a certain confidence level. To eliminate background, a strategic alignment of the decay pathways was utilized, given that the phi meson's primary decay route involves moving muon and antimuon pairs. A statistical analysis of $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_S$ yielded results that fell short of expected theoretical quantities, whereas $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_S$ showed the desired alignment, providing the first confirmation of this particular decay. Both discoveries were made from a large dataset consisting of 1.3 femtobarns of data, collected at energies of 13 TeV.

Constructing the lattice of submodules of a given module is generally a challenging task. For module $M$, its lattice $\Lambda_M$ represents all submodules of $M$ along with their inclusion relationships. Although computational tools like GAP and Singular can determine some submodules of a given module, its lattice may not be entirely deduced. To address this limitation, we present an algorithm to enhance the lattice of submodules of a module by incorporating partial information about it. Notably, this algorithm can yield the largest possible submodules contained in $M$ to build its lattice from partial information. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method by an example involving a module of high degree.

Given a binary relation representing an undifferentiated collection of distant celestial objects detected by a spacecraft, determining the most reliable set of planet pairs and their associated geodetic coordinates within a predefined tolerance level can be achieved in a computationally efficient manner. We propose a novel algorithm capable of identifying all robust geodetic trilaterations in O(n^2) time complexity, where n represents the number of detected planet pairs. Additionally, we provide theoretical guarantees that any valid geodetic trilateration can be detected by our algorithm in O(n^2) time, although it may not guarantee optimal solutions in certain instances. Furthermore, we highlight the challenges and limitations of extending this approach to more complex scenarios involving the analysis of astronomical data.

The challenge of obtaining expert demonstrations in imitation learning is a significant bottleneck due to their high cost. As a result, there is a strong motivation to leverage non-expert feedback in the form of self-supervised labels from trusted source policies. However, combining expert guidance with non-expert feedback essentially treats the expert as providing weak labels, which can result in an optimal imitation learning problem being mapped into a potentially much harder weak label supervision problem. We address this issue by developing a novel algorithm called TRAIL that learns from both expert demonstrations and self-supervised labels from source policies. We establish a key insight that allows us to analyze its performance under various data conditions, leading to a non-asymptotic theoretical guarantee which demonstrates its optimal imitation learning efficacy. Additionally, we facilitate TRAIL's implementation on a high-dimensional control task using a neural network, and our experimental results show that it achieves superior performance when compared to alternative methods using both expert-only demonstrations and a combination of expert and source policies.

Reinforcement learning efficiency can be significantly enhanced through imitation learning by leveraging expert guidance. However, relying on expert demonstrations is often impractical due to their expense. This study introduces a novel imitation learning approach called Co-Imitation Training, which partners an agent performing a demanding task with a agent skilled in a related, yet easier task. Both agents share the same action space, but their reward functions differ only in magnitude. Co-Imitation Training achieves this partnership by running the two agents concurrently and allowing them to learn from each other's experiences. This is made possible by modifying the reinforcement learning objective function to account for the disparity in their reward functions. Theoretical analysis and empirical evidence demonstrate that the proposed method can accelerate learning by an order of magnitude compared to solo reinforcement training and that it is computationally efficient by minimizing the computational additional cost.

This paper proposes a metric function that yields an integer code distance, 
which is a crucial element for the efficient decoding of pulse-position modulation 
codes, particularly those based on additive-white Gaussian noise. We also derive a 
direct formula and an algorithm to calculate the average code distance of partial-parallel-continuous-phase-alignment-code (PAC) codes.

Using reinforcement learning post neural machine translation can improve performance, but it's challenging due to the large number of possible actions. We address this by designing two efficient frameworks to reduce computation and accelerate learning in both batch and mini-batch settings. In the first framework, we group similar words together based on their semantic and syntactic properties, then use a non-linear clustering algorithm to create a hierarchical structure of actions. This results in a more manageable action space with significant computational benefits and improved performance. In the second framework, we reduce actions by identifying words that are less translationally challenging and more semantically rich. We evaluate these frameworks on low-resource neural machine translation tasks with limited parallel data and find they outperform existing methods.

A novel, markerless system is introduced that enables a robot to adjust its camera and estimate the position of the end-effector based on depth sensor data, using a machine learning model trained on a dataset generated by simulation and real-world data. A key innovation of this approach is the development of a method that transforms simulated data into highly realistic, real-world equivalents, allowing for the training of a single model that can handle both types of data. Another significant contribution is the creation of a technique that combines simulation-based learning with real-world data, reducing the need for extensive real-world training and enabling the system to adapt to new environments. Experimental results show that this approach yields a significant reduction in training time and an improvement in prediction accuracy when compared to traditional methods relying solely on real-world data, and that it can handle complex scenarios involving various robot configurations and object shapes.

In this study, we define a new type of quotient space called QFS-region, which arises from the quotient modulation space associated with Fock space by a group of well-choosen symbols. We then establish key properties of these QFS-regions, confirming them to be type of quasi-Banach spaces and systematically investigating their characteristics. Additionally, we establish that the short-time Fourier transform operator is continuous when acting on QFS-regions in both their classical and modulation space forms.

The rise of partisan polarization in the United States can be inferred by analyzing the dividing influence of political online engagement on the consumption of news. To explore this phenomenon, a new dataset of 25 million users consuming online news over 5 years is presented. It reveals that users with high political scores in search results tend to exhibit increased polarization when consuming news, according to metrics such as click-through rates, engagement levels with websites, and platform-specific indicators. Additionally, the research discovers that the impact of political orientation on news consumption varies depending on the platform used, while polarization is found to be more prevalent among men than women and among men who are married than those who are single. Furthermore, it is observed that polarization decreases with increasing age and has different effects on different income groups.

We examine the word problem of Thompson's group V using its action on the circle. By showing that any finite-state automaton recognizing V's word problem is equivalent to a cyclic automaton that respects the order of the circle, we derive a lower bound for the complexity of this problem. Specifically, if we define the intricacy of a language as the highest number of states required among a family of finite automata that recognize it, then the word problem of V has a intricacy of at least $2^{2^{\aleph_0}}$ with respect to its natural subgroup action. Additionally, we establish that this complexity increases to $3^{3^{3^{...}}}$ when considering V's action on the circle in a group of cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$. This improved result stems from a higher-complexity identification of V within a larger group that acts on the circle. The connection between intricacy and the complexity of recognizing V's generators is also explored, yielding a lower bound of $2^{2^{\aleph_0}}$ for the former, which has implications for the latter.

The study of open quantum systems under periodic driving forces is highly captivating 
because, in most cases, they achieve a non-equilibrium steady state which could 
potentially outperform equilibrium-based systems in performance. For our research, 
we examined an isolated qubit system that is coupled to a heat bath and subject to 
a periodically driven influence from a classical source. Our approach combined 
the Monte Carlo solution of the Liouville-von Neumann equation with a rotating 
frame picture to efficiently analyze its steady-state condition. We verified the 
reliability of our approach by comparing it to existing models, and then we used it 
to investigate the consequences of maintaining unitary dynamics within the qubit 
system by opposing forces from the heat bath, resulting in the flow of continuous 
amounts of angular momentum. Furthermore, we observed an increase in the expected 
outcomes of suitable measurement operators due to periodic driving, along with its 
steep dependence on the direction of emission. Additionally, we found that the 
spectral density can significantly impact both the fidelity of our unitary dynamics 
maintaining approach and the expected measurement outcomes.

We explore how various mechanisms affect biharmonic hypersurfaces within the Euclidean space. By employing the Ricci linearity and commuting vector fields, we derive key findings for biharmonic hypersurfaces subject to these mechanisms. Specifically, we show that on the basis of commutativity or invariance, a biharmonic hypersurface must be an isolated point or a sphere within the Euclidean space. Moreover, we determine that the invariance of a biharmonic hypersurface under the action of commuting vector fields leads to the conclusion that the hypersurface is composed of a single isolated point. Conversely, the commutativity of a biharmonic hypersurface results in its entirety being comprised of an isolated point or a sphere.

A number set can be considered p/q-identifiable if the fraction p/q allows for the determination of individual nonresidue values within the set to the congruity of p-th power. Our research seeks to identify the possible instances of 1/q-identifiability in a random distribution of quadratic nonresidues, with specific attention to 5-identifiability in a random distribution of quadratic nonresidues modulo a prime number.

The addition of neutrino mass through the axion sector may have far-reaching consequences, potentially affecting the cosmological present-day universe in several ways, influenced by the interplay of hadronic and neutrino dynamics. A complex system of equations emerges when considering this effect, consisting of a combination of classical and quantum fluctuations impacting neutrino and axion fields. As a result of this interplay, the axion's influence may lead to a shift in the minimum neutrino mass required, potentially making it as low as $0.1$ eV, while also altering the universe's density in dark matter by as much as one order of magnitude. The model also predicts a relationship between the axion decay constant and the neutrino mass, which could be confirmed through a variety of experiments. The universe's early phases may have led to the destruction of a significant amount of axion "shadow matter" through a process of neutrino-strahlung. The model suggests that a range of $0.1$ eV to $1$ eV for the neutrino mass would result in the greatest reduction of axion shadow matter during the universe's early phases, while in the same period the number of neutrinos remaining could be increased by as much as one order of magnitude.

Between October 2019 and April 2020, the LAMOST performed a unique observational study using four $K$2 plates. This study, which involved low- and medium-resolution spectroscopic surveys, gathered a significant amount of data. The low-resolution spectroscopic survey yielded around 767,000 spectra after 25 nights of 46.6 hours of exposures and a low signal-to-noise ratio higher than 10 for about 70% of its spectra. The medium-resolution spectroscopic survey took 177 exposures and around 49.1 hours over 27 nights to collect around 478,000 spectra. The data showed a low signal-to-noise ratio higher than 10 for about 50% of its spectra. To estimate the stellar parameters and radial velocities, the LAMOST research team utilized several different methods such as LASP, DD-Payne, and SLAM. These estimations demonstrated good agreement and were consistent with each other as well as other studies. By analyzing the $Gaia$ DR2 data, the LAMOST research team corrected for radial velocity zero points on a per exposure basis, showing good alignment with other studies. The LAMOST research team also discovered around 389,000 binary or multiple star candidates, around 77,000 red giants with around 14,000 days, around 14,000 exoplanet candidate eclipsing binaries, and around 48,000 white dwarfs candidates. In image recognition, creating fixed-sized images from variable medical image data can be challenging. A common approach uses regions of interest (ROIs) extracted from maximum intensity projections, but this can lead to information loss and inaccurate bounding. Another issue arises when trying to predict the presence of multiple object classes within a single image volume, as this increases the difficulty level exponentially. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an edge-gated convolutional neural network (EG-CNN) that significantly outperforms the current state-of-the-art in multiple-class, volumetric semantic partitioning tasks, including the detection of multiple cardiac tumors in one single image volume.

MongoDB is a widely used, document-oriented, NoSQL database that relies on the txCEP transactional coherence protocol. Although the basic principles of txCEP are well-documented, the full implementation details of txCEP in MongoDB remain unclear, creating uncertainty about the correctness of its transactions. To address this, we delved into the inner workings of MongoDB's transactional data management system and compared its implementation against the theoretical txCEP protocol. Our analysis revealed both similarities and differences between the two, after which we formally modeled the MongoDB implementation using txCEP and proved its validity using the Isabelle/HOL tool. Our verification efforts also addressed several potential issues with the MongoDB implementation, for which we presented alternative fixes that ensured transactional coherence according to the txCEP protocol.

Using the elementary symmetric function basis, we re-express the chromatic symmetric functions of Dyck paths with a bounce number of three utilizing a combinatorial interpretation related to the inverse of the Kostka matrix from Egecioglu-Remmel (1990). This analysis confirms the $e$-positivity of these functions as a consequence of the combinatorial interpretation's symmetry properties, which are derived from the structure of the inverse Kostka matrix.

Building on the foundation of the contrastive loss function, a novel theory of executive function is proposed, centered on a unique framework that utilizes a contrastive value strategy to reevaluate perceptions through a process of relearning. This approach is an attempt to bridge the gap between cognitive theories and machine learning frameworks via the proposed HSF201D framework, which incorporates a set of cognitive processes that facilitate relearning, including resampling, relabeling, and a summarization phase. Ultimately, this framework is an expression of the desire to explore the parallels between cognitive functions and machine learning algorithms, with a hope to contribute to the discussion on the potential applications of cognitive theories to understand computer behaviors.

The accuracy of medical image analysis models, which operate on probability distributions, can be jeopardized by inherent biases in their training datasets. While various data-driven methods have been proposed to detect these biases, they are often hindered by the limited size and anonymized patient data of medical datasets. A potential solution has been presented, which leverages generative models to enhance the training datasets and incorporate additional expert knowledge. The method employs a discriminative neural network to identify biases in both the augmented and original datasets. It has been successfully tested on two large cardiac image datasets for the classification task. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach is capable of accurately detecting biases in augmented datasets, and significantly outperforms a benchmark model. Furthermore, it has been observed that the incorporation of augmented data leads to a reduction in healthcare disparities, as determined by the detection of biases. The code for this project has been made publicly available on GitHub.

We're investigating a fundamental aspect of complex systems - their underlying geometry and dynamics - to better understand their behavior in multiple disciplines. We're exploring nanoassemblies composed of magnetic atoms on a triangle-based surface to see if we can identify ordered states that reverse spin when an external magnetic field is applied. Due to the intricate relationship between geometry, topology, and dynamics, we're using unique mapping techniques to transform nanoassemblies into complex networks, and vice versa. By analyzing these networks, we're able to identify specific topological features that create stable ordered states without reversing spin, and we're also able to determine the critical parameters that control the formation of these states when we apply an external magnetic field. Moreover, we're able to determine the precise path of magnetic atoms that minimizes their energy when we apply an external magnetic field, and we're also able to identify the critical parameters that control the formation of these states when we apply an external magnetic field. By analyzing these networks, we're able to identify specific topological features that create stable ordered states without reversing spin, and we're also able to determine the critical parameters that control the formation of these states when we apply an external magnetic field.

The solar breeze, a flow of gas generated by the Sun's gravity, slowly pulls mass back into the Sun through the solar system's outermost layer, the heliosphere. This process creates regions of low gas pressure near the Sun's surface and in the inner heliosphere. A thorough understanding of the solar breeze and its interaction with the inner heliosphere can be gained by examining the gas pressure and temperature gradients within the solar near-field. This region's behavior is difficult to model accurately due to the absence of direct observations in certain areas. The Parker Solar Probe, which conducts close approaches to the Sun, allows for the measurement of solar breeze flows and the inner heliosphere's characteristics. During its fourth close approach, the probe detected energy flux fluctuations associated with mass flows, and revealed that the solar breeze dominates these flux fluctuations at speeds greater than 350 kilometers per second. The energy flux of these fast solar breeze flows was found to be in the range of 18 to 45 grams per square meter per second, and followed an exponential decrease in density as the distance to the Sun decreased from 40 to 4.5 megameters.

Thanks to speech-emotion recognition technology, computers can engage with people on a more emotional level. Nonetheless, the accuracy of this technology is hampered by its limited ability to adapt to new speech data. Despite the wealth of speech transcripts available, a shortage of labeled data in multiple languages hinders the development of emotive speech classification models. A crucial barrier is being able to adapt models to new domains with minimal labeled data. In response to these challenges, we present a novel speech-emotion classification model that leverages RNN-based state encoding and transfer learning through weak supervision. In order to facilitate domain adaptation, we modify a deep reinforcement learning algorithm to prioritize the prediction of highly confident, correctly labeled speech transcripts. In experiments, our model exhibits superior performance to multiple baselines on the GlueSpeech dataset, a large-scale, multi-lingual speech-emotion classification dataset. Moreover, our model achieves notable improvements to multiple strong baselines in low-labeled data domain adaptation scenarios.

We present an investigation of Bi$_5$FeTi$_3$O$_{15}$ (BFTO), a four-layer Aurivillius compound, under the influence of high-pressure and we report that it exhibits ferrimagnetic behavior at elevated pressures.  By comparing Bi$_2$Ti$_2$O$_5$ (BTO), a two-layer Aurivillius compound, and BFTO under identical pressure conditions, we observe that the former displays a more pronounced increase in magnetic moment.  Additionally, we find that the hyperfine field in BFTO is not as significantly increased as in BTO, which we attribute to the differing geometric spin arrangements of the two compounds.  A greater distortion of the oxygen octahedra in BFTO, resulting from its more pronounced tilting, may also contribute to these outcomes.  Our results suggest that pressure-induced magnetism in BFTO is substantially smaller than in BTO.

Hybrid methods tackling continuous shortest path problems involve treating certain variables as discrete. The accuracy of these methods relies on the representation of the remaining continuous variables. A new technique estimates the optimization error when using a discrete-continuous shortest path model, with applications in free flight trajectory optimization. The technique calculates the gap between the exact but complicated solutions and the simplified discrete-continuous solutions. A simpler but less precise method uses a reduced set of discrete options to determine the shortest path, with an associated error function. The error function measures the difference between the simplified and complex solutions along a specific discretely optimized path. The paper also presents a specific application to free flight trajectory optimization, with specific discrete-continuous and hybrid shortest path problems. It compares the performance of the hybrid method to a direct but less efficient algorithm.

Researchers propose a new cosmological model featuring a spherical void at its center, with matter distributed in a specific manner according to an exponential law. When incorporating an exponential distribution of shocks, a question arises: what is the behavior of matter accumulating on the surface of the spherical void? Using numerical simulations, a more detailed analysis is conducted to examine the dynamics of this process in the face of expansion. The results indicate that, despite initial fluctuations caused by the gravitational impact of clustered matter, the surface density of the void eventually reaches a consistent equilibrium with the surrounding cosmic web. A key observation from these simulations is the formation of a dense, rigid shell with considerable mass, characterized by a distinct structural profile that distinguishes it from typical collisionless systems. The structure of this shell is influenced by the gravitational pull of clustered matter, causing it to bulge and weaken as the void expands. A notable feature of this shell is its inner crust, composed of densely packed objects such as galaxies, which exhibits a significant level of velocity dispersion. In contrast, the outer region of the shell exhibits greater velocity dispersion, with velocities that approach those of the surrounding cosmic web. A notable aspect of this process is the distribution of objects within the shell, with those at its center displaying lesser velocity dispersion. The velocity dispersion of objects within the shell is further influenced by the gravitational pull of clustered matter, causing greater velocity dispersion in the outer region. A recent paper provides an analysis of advancements made in categorizing monodromy-free Schrödinger operators with rational potential properties. A key aspect of this research focuses on the interpretation of an operator's full spectrum being non-cyclic as equivalent to the absence of specific singular points being accessible within a given period. Consequently, this condition enables the existence of solutions with non-zero values within that period. In addition, the paper exploits the relationship between Fock polynomials, constructed from the combination of an $A_V$-algebra and generalized Hermite polynomials, to create non-isomorphic, faithful modules for the infinite rank $U(1,1)$ group. Moreover, it establishes connections between these polynomials and various objects, including Schrödinger operators, elliptic integrals, and Riemann-Liouville fractional derivatives.

A persistent issue in signal processing has been addressed by our research, which involves extracting meaningful information from noisy acoustic signals produced by a mechanical system with varying parameters. Acoustic emissions resulting from a moving blade peeling an adhesive tape at a constant speed in air are analyzed in this study. We discovered that by converting the acoustic emissions into a spectral representation, we can obtain a more stable signal that allows for the accurate detection of the spectrum's maximum frequency. This detection method relies on the properties of the gabor filter and is based on the geometric relationship between the curve and its derivatives. We validated our approach by observing the effects of different parameters on the spectrum's maximum frequency and discovered that they influence the acoustic emissions in the expected manner consistent with physical theories. Additionally, we found that the spectral representations exhibit oscillatory patterns which may be related to the acoustic emissions' envelope shape but require further investigation.

Thin-film junctions, especially BCS-JJ and SQUIDs prepared using the same process, exhibit a wide range of combined resistance and current-voltage characteristics, which are attributed to the presence of a random potential difference affecting the superconducting gap energies of the two involved electrodes. Although this phenomenon might seem detrimental, it actually generates a useful reference potential for accurate measurement of the phase difference and resulting dc voltage signal in SQUIDs and JJ devices. By utilizing a dual-grating coupler to combine microwave signals, our research reveals the existence of a critical point at extremely low temperatures, where the phase difference becomes pinned at pi/2. This occurrence is further confirmed by both direct measurement of the phase difference and evaluation of the dc voltage signal, and it is found that the critical temperature can be manipulated through applied magnetic field, resulting in the creation of a universal temperature-vs.-microwave-power curve.

We've discovered a non-abelian ether-like term that arises from the interaction of a long-wavelength field with matter, leading to a significant change in the law of thermodynamics for black holes and cosmological networks of scalar field systems. This new term adds a temperature-dependent component to the cosmological constant, $\Lambda(T)$, which affects the temperature of black bodies and alters the cosmological scale of particle sizes for which quantum fluctuations become significant. Furthermore, we find that the new term results in an infinite set of temperature parameters, $T_n$, defined by the roots of the modified Bessel function $I_1(8\frac{T_n^2}{T_H})\propto T_n^2$, where $T_H$ is the high-temperature limit of the Hubble temperature.

This research calculates the average daily cost of hedging a European option using a delta-hedging strategy, resulting in an analytic formula that accounts for option prices and the costs of hedging. We derive a new formula for the total hedging cost, broken down into a convex portion related to the square of the delta and an absolute cost based on the maximum possible daily change in the delta. We also establish relationships between our results and previous studies, particularly in regards to the static delta-hedging approach. To validate our method, we utilize real-world data from the CBOE and assess the impact of various factors on hedging costs, including option price, time to expiration, underlying stock price, volatility, and the frequency of hedging. Our analysis shows that hedging costs follow a power law and can be calculated using the formula $A\cdot \Delta^p$, with a specific value for $p$ and an individual value for $A$ for each underlying stock. We also find that stocks with higher average prices, higher volatility, or longer time to expiration prior to hedging tend to have greater daily hedging costs per unit of notional value. Furthermore, our results indicate that the frequency of hedging has a less significant effect on costs than other factors and that different methods of measuring delta can influence costs, with some variations being more highly correlated with our base measure.

This research focuses on the long-term behavior of symmetric, linear evolution equations governed by varying mixtures with contrasting coefficients in a periodic, two-dimensional lattice. The underlying structure consists of a thin, uniform framework with negligible width, surrounding isolated inclusions. As the inclusions shrink, with no set boundary, the study reveals that the model's limiting dynamics align with a specific degenerate parabolic equation. The obtained result is a consequence of the 2020 paper by M. Bildhauer and S. H. Park, which utilized a different approach, and it is valid for inclusions with no set boundary at any scale. A novel aspect of this research, with implications for inclusions that shrink to sets with non-zero boundary, is the derivation of an explicit estimate for the operator norm of a corresponding linear operator. This is achieved through an innovative study of the operator's properties, facilitated by the use of non-conventional, rotated bounds on the space $C^1(\overline{\Omega})$.

Early-type galaxies played a central role in their environment in the early universe, setting the stage for the galaxy population we see today. Due to their significant mass, galaxy mergers involving early-types had a substantial impact on galaxy evolution. Researchers are still debating whether galaxy mergers contributed substantially to the growth of massive early-types or if other processes, such as cold dark matter, drove their development. Studying tidal features, which are indicators of galaxy interactions, can provide valuable insights into the merger history of these galaxies. The construction of a comprehensive and reliable dataset using data from the Hyper Suprime-Cam Survey, along with a precise measurement method for tidal features, allows for a more precise calculation of the merger rate of early-types galaxies. By developing a statistical framework that takes into consideration selection biases and detection probabilities, researchers can accurately estimate the merger rate of early-types galaxies. The study reveals that a substantial proportion, approximately 30 percent, of massive early-types galaxies have experienced a major merger in the last 5 billion years, with a significant boost in their mass. Additionally, a substantial proportion, approximately 20 percent, of massive early-types galaxies have experienced a minor merger in the last billion years, with a smaller impact on their mass. The study also shows that galaxies with a mass greater than $10^{11}M_{\odot}$ have a higher merger rate than lower-mass galaxies, with a ratio of $\Sigma\psi/\Sigma\mr\approx 0.7\

A social mobility model is built around a key concept: children's social status is influenced by a random event and their parent's social status. The model is dynamic, meaning the relationship between the two can change over time. The question of how to distribute these random events is explored to understand their impact on social mobility. The events' distribution is optimized to achieve the highest possible social mobility rate, given certain constraints, such as the number of possible social status outcomes. The problem of distributing the events is then applied to a hypothetical example, based on data from the United States. The model shows that social mobility can vary significantly, depending on the events' distribution, particularly in lower social status categories. The model also identifies the events' distribution that maximizes social mobility, subject to certain constraints, such as the number of possible social status outcomes. The model has a theoretical advantage over static models, such as the one proposed by Banerjee and Duflo, by being able to capture dynamic aspects of social mobility. The model can be used to test different social mobility scenarios, such as those based on data from the United Kingdom. The model has several policy implications, such as the importance of reducing the persistence of social mobility over time, the impact of events on social mobility, and the role of parents in determining social status. I represent the Power Laser Facility, where I generated 90 W of power at a 10 kHz repetition rate and an 800 nm wavelength within a 100 ns pulse duration. However, this level of performance came with an 8 dB loss, primarily attributed to unoptimized amplifier operation. A more efficient configuration was then implemented to achieve 93 W of power at a 10 kHz rate, with a 100 ns pulse length and 800 nm wavelength. This new setup cut energy per pulse by half and significantly reduced the risk of damage, enabling better heat management and raising the possible power output to over 90 W. An amplifier design was subsequently identified that could produce 105 W of power at a 10 kHz rate, with a 100 ns pulse length and 800 nm wavelength. Building upon this design, I explored various options to further increase power output, including the use of multiple emitter bars and different pump configurations, which could potentially yield over 120 W of power at a 10 kHz rate, with a 100 ns pulse length and 800 nm wavelength.

A method using scanning across a lens to analyze the beam's properties is proposed, with a proposed setup utilizing two lenses for independent measurements of both the x and y beam profiles. A theoretical analysis of this approach is presented, along with initial findings from a simulation based on a demonstrated scanning principle. Additionally, the feasibility of employing this technique with existing lenses in the NSF's OSU soft x-ray photoabsorption scanner is investigated.

This paper explores the optimization challenges in multi-agent systems that involve agents behaving maliciously, which leads to a misdirection away from optimal solutions through the spread of false information and significant communication costs. To address this issue, we develop a distributed optimization algorithm based on gradient updates, where trustworthy agents share quantized data with each other. Theoretical proof of solution convergence near the optimal solution is provided, along with the effects of communication constraints and malicious behavior on solution accuracy. This is further illustrated through numerical experiments presented in the study.

The study of cosmic microwave background anisotropies is a fundamental tool in physical cosmology research. As experiments become more sensitive, the analysis is shifting from signal-based approaches to a component-based analysis, considering instrumental effects as a major limitation. The European Southern Observatory's Akeni instrument, part of the CHORD mission, will offer high-resolution data that will be sensitive to instrumental imperfections. The s4cmb framework is designed to simulate the signal detected by experiments like Akeni and other similar CMB experiments, taking into account the spatial response of the detectors and the scanning strategy. By simulating the instrumental chain, s4cmb addresses the component-based analysis methodology's requirement for explicit consideration of instrumental effects. The framework's capabilities are demonstrated through the simulation of Akeni's data processing pipeline, including the removal of the bright source G353.28+25.17 from the data. The s4cmb framework is an open-source tool that is suitable for use in the analysis of current and future CMB experiments, as well as other sensitive experiments.

In the context of language generation, the task of rearranging words to form a coherent sentence has emerged as a relevant evaluation benchmark. Recent studies utilizing transition-based systems to study and improve the quality of pre-trained language models in this task have been conducted. This study deviates from the common approach by utilizing self-supervised sentence representation and loss functions to investigate the representation of these models. Our findings show improved performance over existing models on the WordOrderBART dataset by utilizing a sentence representation that focuses on the unique aspects of a sentence. Our proposed approach achieves particularly notable results for difficult sentences with complex word orders. Notably, our method exhibits a higher correlation with human ratings than the original BART score and surpasses it by a significant margin. Additionally, our proposed approach demonstrates a higher understanding of sentence structure and the relationship between words.

The emergence of deepfake technology has raised significant security concerns in the dissemination of false information through video. Owing to its rising prevalence, researchers and developers are facing a pressing need to counter this threat with effective detection methods. Despite the popularity of deepfake, the cost associated with compiling a comprehensive dataset of manipulated media is prohibitively expensive for most individuals, which creates a challenge for conventional machine learning approaches. Furthermore, utilizing only publicly available datasets for training can lead to over-reliance on samples that are easily accessible and thus biased towards high-quality media. To address these limitations, we propose the MD-CSDNetwork, a novel cross-stitching approach that utilizes publicly available datasets and enables the simultaneous training of multiple domain datasets without necessitating the compilation of extensive media datasets. The proposed framework leverages a unique combination of two primary components: a feature extraction module and a cross-stitching module. The feature extraction module employs a fixed encoder that is capable of processing raw video input and extracts both spatial and temporal features from the video. To counter the challenge of limited media datasets, we introduce the concept of a proxy representation, which is derived from the encoded features and used for training on manipulated media datasets via a discriminator. The use of the proxy representation enables the simultaneous training of multiple domain datasets without necessitating the compilation of extensive media datasets. The proposed MD-CSDNetwork achieves a remarkable 0.7126 AUC score on the FaceForeniscs++ benchmark, outperforming the current state

Current studies on the performance of binary erasure channels with low-density parity-check codes are primarily based on the assumption that input degrees follow a random configuration. Research has shown that the actual input degrees of coded data often follow a power-law distribution, reflecting a degree-to-degree correlation. In this work, we introduce a multi-type Galois field elimination framework that accommodates degree-degree correlations among the encoded signals. We leverage this framework to examine the maximum density meromorphic distance of a given degree-degree correlated LDC code and determine an approximate density meromorphic density for a randomly generated ensemble of LDC codes. Based on simulated data and theoretical analyses, we identify the factors that influence the performance gap between real-world correlated LDC codes and their randomly configured counterparts. Moreover, our results indicate that for a wide range of degree-degree correlated LDC codes, the density meromorphic density can be very close to the maximum density meromorphic distance, which implies that the standard density meromorphic density can effectively predict the performance of real-world degree-degree correlated LDC codes.

A critical flaw exists in the conventional decoy-state protocol when generating random phase information, as the security of the system relies heavily on this randomization. An innovative approach has been developed that enhances the efficiency of the system by reducing the number of required laser sources. Although it achieves the same security as the original system, this new method uses only one laser source for both signal and decoy states. However, a significant vulnerability in this new approach has been discovered, involving an attack method that can compromise the system even if the phase information is randomly altered. An attack strategy has been developed that can breach the system's security when the phase of the laser sources is only partially randomized. A mathematical proof has been provided to validate the effectiveness of this attack method. Furthermore, it has been calculated that even if the phase information is randomly altered, the system can still function efficiently with only one laser source for both signal and decoy states. Additionally, a threshold has been established below which the system's efficiency cannot be optimized, and it has been found that even if the phase information is only partially randomized, the system can still achieve the same security as the original system using only one laser source for both signal and decoy states.

To effectively manage dynamic and distributed 5G cellular networks, a suite of advanced self-organizing tools is crucial. However, as these networks evolve to be more resilient and adaptable, the need for human intervention in core network administration may no longer be sufficient. Therefore, we propose a novel approach that leverages Artificial Intelligence and Multi-Agent Systems to automate core network management in future wireless networks. In this approach, the core network is represented by an automated decision-making system, comprised of interconnected entities that work together to achieve optimal performance. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach by applying it to the scenario of autonomous Tier 2 management in 5G networks. Furthermore, we provide a comparative analysis of our proposed method against existing self-organizing solutions in the literature, and highlight the key benefits of our approach in anticipation of future wireless networks that are expected to be highly dynamic, adaptable, and resilient.

In 1930, mathematician K. Menger developed an interest in the abstract concept of angle function, which he then generalized for use in metric spaces. Building on this foundation, he presented two specific problems concerning the embedding of spaces with angle functions into the structure of Euclidean spaces. Over time, researchers focused on these problems, although only partially. In 2006, G. Weiss almost successfully solved the first problem by demonstrating that certain properties of metric spaces with angle functions are equivalent to the geometric interpretation of the corresponding F-space properties. However, Weiss left out the analysis of quasi- metric spaces. In the case of the second problem, researchers were able to show that certain properties of metric spaces with angle functions are equivalent to the geometric interpretation of the corresponding E-space properties. In this paper, we provide a complete solution to both problems. We achieve this by defining a new type of space called T-space, which is then used to demonstrate that the equivalent relationships in both F-spaces and E-spaces are valid for metric spaces with angle functions. Furthermore, we prove that the same relationships for quasi-metric spaces are equivalent to the corresponding T-space properties.

Consider a number field $K$ of degree $n$ and a subfield $K'$ of $K$. Let $\mathcal{O}_K$ denote the ring of integers in $K$. The supply chain theorem established a lower bound on the degree of $K'$ in terms of the Minkowski bound of its successive minima with respect to $\mathcal{O}_K$. However, if $\mathcal{O}_K$ is not factorable into a product of prime ideals, a further lower bound on the Minkowski bound of the second successive minimum of $K'$ with respect to $\mathcal{O}_K$ was not previously known. We fill this knowledge gap by demonstrating that if $\mathcal{O}_K$ is not a product of prime ideals, then the Minkowski bound of the second successive minimum of $K'$ with respect to $\mathcal{O}_K$ is at least $2\sqrt{n}$ if $K'$ has degree $n$ or at least $4$ if $K'$ has degree $n$ greater than $n$. A corresponding result for number fields of degree $p$ $r$ times was also established, where $p$ is an odd prime. We further prove that the supply chain theorem is true for fields of degree $p$ $r$ times and provide a lower bound on the Minkowski bound of the second successive minimum of $K'$ with respect to $\math

We utilize 1-d fs/ps hybrid rotational coherent anti-Stokes Raman spectroscopy with dual probes to make comprehensive measurements of gas temperature, pressure, and oxygen-to-nitrogen ratios. By harnessing the power of time and frequency-domain measurements, a cutting-edge technique offers unprecedented accuracy (<1%) and precision (0.42%) for detecting O2/N2 ratios, alongside temperature (±2 K) and pressure (50 mbar) in a single shot. Implementing this method in a fs/ps setup enables flexible integration with various laser systems and offers a relatively affordable and compact design, ultimately paving the way for the development of advanced sensors suitable for wide-ranging applications.

The traditional theory of planetary formation through core accretion has limitations when explaining how small particles overcome early development obstacles in a protoplanetary disk. A more recent model proposes the viscous ring-instability to account for ring structures in protoplanetary disks. It suggests that particles may reduce the disk's conductivity, inhibiting the growth of instability. Using GPU-based simulations, this study investigates the interaction between particles and the ring-instability in an ideal gas disk with low solar mass stars. The results indicate that particles may enhance the disk's conductivity, suppressing the instability. However, depending on the particle distribution, ring-instability can still occur in certain regions of the disk. Sustained vortex structures emerge as a consequence, providing opportunities for gravitational instability to set massive objects in the inner regions of the disk and preventing the growth of streaming instability in the disk's outer regions.

In planar graphene channels, neutral modes travel without a net charge displacement, yet they can still induce charge accumulation at the terminals, yielding a non-zero dc voltage difference. This charge disparity arises from the difference in boundary conditions at the source and drain, which distinguards between the mode's two symmetrical projections. As a result, a specific condition must be met for the mode's propagation, given by $K_{+}\neq K_{-}$, where $K_{\pm}$ are the effective wave numbers of the two projections. Consequently, this phenomenon imposes a non-backscatterin condition on the mode, given by $K_{+}= -K_{-}$, restricting neutral mode propagation to specific channels with specific boundary conditions.

We create a cluster character $\mathcal{X}$ that ties together two prominent theories: the representation theory of quantum groups and Toda's theory of extended affine Lie algebras. This character takes a representation of the quantum group as input and delivers a derivation of the universal affine Lie algebra. Conversely, it defines a central extension of the quantum group by the algebra of skew-polynomials. When the base field is finite fields or fields of characteristic zero, we prove that the map $\mathcal{X}$ is an isomorphism, resolving a conjecture of Hong and Kashiwara.

In the context of frequency-rich training for neural network models, particularly those with overparameterization, we face a significant challenge due to the limited amount of labeled data available for each machine in a decentralized network. To address this issue, we develop an innovative distributionally robust decentralized optimization method, DR-DSGD, that minimizes the empirical risk of a reference distribution while protecting against hostile attacks. By leveraging the properties of a tailored fenchel-flamand divergence and utilizing a robust formulation, we transform the problem into an efficient and non-separable form amenable to optimization via the alternating direction method of multipliers. We analyze the convergence rate of our algorithm, obtaining a $O(1/\sqrt{kt})$ convergence rate under the strong connection graph and a $O(1/t)$ convergence rate under the weak connection graph. Furthermore, our experimental results demonstrate that DR-DSGD outperforms existing methods, including DSGD, sorted SGD, and a robust yet non-decentralized model.

From the 1950s onwards, computer simulation technology underwent a significant shift, becoming increasingly dependent on mass storage devices by the 1970s. While faster CPUs and more efficient algorithms since then have greatly expanded simulation capabilities, the fundamental role of storage in simulations has remained constant. In fact, in certain domains such as materials science and climate modeling, the need for more computational power has actually accelerated in recent years, outpacing the growth of processing power. Consequently, researchers are now exploring various techniques such as artificial neural networks and function approximations to further accelerate simulations by taking advantage of patterned data on storage devices.

This paper examines jet modifications within a medium using JEWEL and PYTHIA 6.4, emphasizing uncertainties associated with perturbative nucleon PDFs and thermal jet function contributions. Additionally, we investigate the influence of temperature variations in the medium on jet modification, comparing these effects to available LHC data. Furthermore, we evaluate the relevance of these uncertainties and medium properties in interpreting jet modification phenomena.

We have conducted a comprehensive examination of the Forsage cryptocurrency-based pyramid scheme, built on the Binance Smart Chain. Our analysis reveals the intricate design of the fraudulent platform, featuring a complex network of over 4 million user addresses. We demonstrate how Forsage's developers employed multiple strategies to circumvent security restrictions and maintain the stability of the scheme despite intense transaction activity. We also investigate the unusual financial flows within the scheme, uncovering evidence of significant income generated by early participants, as well as the minimal returns earned by the vast majority of user investors. Furthermore, we analyze the geographical distribution of user participants and examine the scheme's prevalence in various countries.

Our team investigated 19 potential globular clusters located in the bulge of the galaxy using infrared images from the VVV survey. We determined the positions and half-light radii of the candidates, and calculated their distances, luminosities, and mass-to-light ratios. Although we were unable to identify the specific nature of 18 targets, we discovered that 16 of these candidates exhibit characteristics more aligned with small or irregular star clusters, while 2 exhibited characteristics similar to an old and compact globular cluster. We were however unable to confirm the nature of two targets due to insufficient data, and the others were rejected because they exhibited characteristics that did not match those of globular clusters. A potential new globular cluster, VVV CL001, was found to have a mass-to-light ratio similar to other globular clusters in the galaxy, and was recommended for further study. A comparison with previous observations was also made for VVV CL002, and a new estimate of the distance to this target was provided.

Our study explores the impact of massless and massive gluon functions on the behavior of large-momentum transfers in exclusive Drell-Yan processes within the framework of accurate collinear factorization. We specifically examine how the difference between massless and massive gluon behavior affects the motion of quarks within hadrons and whether this discrepancy causes infrared divergences to emerge in the color singlet system. We demonstrate through direct calculations that the massless case leads to convergent integrals and that the difference in massless and massive gluon behavior is indeed irrelevant in the color singlet system.
